title: Cartesian descent charts for compatible local immersions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For each point $i$ choose an open neighbourhood $U_i$ containing $i$, a scheme $W_i$, and an immersion $j_i:W_i\to U_i$. Assume compatibility: for every scheme $T$, points $i,k$, and maps $a:T\to U_i$, $b:T\to U_k$ with equal composites to $S$, the map $a$ factors through $j_i$ if and only if $b$ factors through $j_k$. Then there exist a scheme $Z$ and a morphism $q:Z\to S$ such that for each $i$ there is a morphism $e_i:W_i\to Z$ making the square with top map $j_i$, left map $e_i$, right map $U_i\to S$, and bottom map $q$ Cartesian. No global factorization criterion or immersion assertion for $q$ is part of this statement.

proof.text: Write f_i = j_i followed by U_i inclusion. The private proved helper compatibleImmersion_openOverlap identifies W_i ×_S W_k with the restriction of W_i to f_i inverse image U_k. Compatibility applied to this restriction gives its map to W_k. The pullback universal property is proved explicitly: an arbitrary cone lifts through the open inclusion, and cancellation of f_k verifies its other component. Hence the pullback first projection is open and its range is precisely f_i inverse image U_k. These steps use Mathlib morphismRestrict_ι, IsOpenImmersion.lift and IsPullback.isoPullback.

The private proved helper exists_gluedMonoOpenAtlas uses the pullbacks W_i ×_S W_j as overlap schemes. Their first projections are open. Pullback symmetry gives transition maps; iterated pullback.lift gives the triple-overlap cyclic permutation. Cancel the monic composite of the two first projections and f_i to prove its cocycle identity. These fields define Scheme.GlueData. Its glued scheme and open charts are jointly surjective. Construct q by Multicoequalizer.desc on the compatible f_i, with compatibility equal to pullback.condition. Multicoequalizer.π_desc proves e_i followed by q = f_i, and GlueData.glue_condition gives equality of the two overlap maps into the gluing.

For z with q(z) in U_i, choose a chart e_k and x with e_k(x)=z. The range formula for the overlap gives a point v of W_k ×_S W_i with first projection x. The overlap chart equality expresses z as e_i of the second projection of v. Thus q inverse image U_i lies in the range of e_i. Given a cone over U_i inclusion and q, lift its Z component through e_i using this range inclusion. Cancel U_i inclusion to prove the other triangle; cancel e_i for uniqueness. This explicitly gives PullbackCone.IsLimit.mk and the required IsPullback. The same construction treats empty S or empty patches without a nonemptiness assumption.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_gluedCompatibleImmersionCharts (S : Scheme.{u})
    (U : S → S.Opens) (hU : ∀ s : S, s ∈ U s)
    (W : S → Scheme.{u}) (j : ∀ s : S, W s ⟶ (U s).toScheme)
    (hj : ∀ s : S, IsImmersion (j s))
    (hcompat : ∀ (i k : S) {T : Scheme.{u}}
      (a : T ⟶ (U i).toScheme) (b : T ⟶ (U k).toScheme),
      a ≫ (U i).ι = b ≫ (U k).ι →
      ((∃ h : T ⟶ W i, h ≫ j i = a) ↔ (∃ h : T ⟶ W k, h ≫ j k = b))) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (q : Z ⟶ S),
      ∀ i : S, ∃ e : W i ⟶ Z, IsPullback (j i) e (U i).ι q
